hooks.text: A massive canyon system on Mars stretches nearly four thousand kilometers long.
The solar system's largest canyon is not located on Earth.
Mars hides an enormous scar that plunges up to eleven kilometers deep.

title: The Martian canyon that crosses an entire planet
description: Discover Valles Marineris, the solar system's largest canyon system that would stretch across the entire continental United States.

beats.text: A massive canyon system on Mars stretches nearly four thousand kilometers long.
beats.visual: Valles Marineris global topography map by MOLA, 2001

beats.text: The historic Mariner 9 mission first revealed this breathtaking Martian scar in nineteen seventy-one.
Its total length is directly comparable to the distance from New York City to Los Angeles.
beats.visual: Tharsis bulge Mars MOLA global relief, 2003

beats.text: The colossal trench plunges up to eleven kilometers deep in certain prominent regions.
beats.visual: Melas Chasma interior mosaic by Mars Express HRSC, 2008

beats.text: Ancient volcanic activity from the Tharsis bulge stressed the planetary crust until it cracked open.
beats.visual: Noctis Labyrinthus fractured terrain by HiRISE, 2010

beats.text: Colossal gravitational landslides then widened the scar, sending debris rushing over a hundred kilometers across.
beats.visual: Candor Chasma layered deposits by HiRISE, 2007
queries: Mars Global Surveyor MOC Candor Chasma

beats.text: Hydrated sulfate minerals like jarosite hide inside this remarkable solar system record breaker.
beats.visual: Coprates Chasma volcanic cones by MRO, 2012
